body.statement: For \(\ell=1\), \(r_{\beta}(1)=3\). On a nonempty relatively Zariski-open subset of \(\mathcal O_{1,3}\), if \(M_3\) has rank two and \(f\ne0\) spans its kernel with \(\operatorname{Cum}(f(X),T,T)\ne0\), then the displayed ratio is defined and every nonempty legal fiber satisfies \(\beta=\operatorname{Cum}(f(X),T,Y)/\operatorname{Cum}(f(X),T,T)\). Tramontano et al., Theorem 3.6, parameterizes the complete modified map \((\beta,\Phi_{1,3})\) and computes its vanishing ideal; the resulting quadratic is reproduced over the full algebraic relaxation \(\mathcal D_{1,3}\). Its additional algebraic beta factor has no lift satisfying \(\mathcal R^{\mathrm{legal}}_{1,3}\): an exact real-infeasibility certificate enforces positive diagonal order-two source variances and one centered representing law for each order-two--three source tuple. The explicitly displayed domain \(\mathcal W_3\) is nonempty, and \(\Psi_3(t)\in\Theta_{1,3}\) for every \(t\in\mathcal W_3\), while \(\Psi_3(t)=\bot\) outside that domain. The explicitly displayed domain \(\mathcal W_2\) is nonempty, and for every \(t\in\mathcal W_2\), \(\Psi_2^{+}(t),\Psi_2^{-}(t)\in\Theta_{1,2}\) are legal independent centered non-Gaussian three-atom source realizations with equal covariance tuples and unequal effects; their common covariance tuples contain a Zariski-dense relatively Euclidean-open subset of \(\mathcal O_{1,2}\).
body.justification: The first exact case both validates the annihilator and prevents algebraic polynomial degree from being mistaken for legal statistical multiplicity.
body.gap: Tramontano et al., Theorem 3.6, correctly computes the vanishing ideal of the complete modified algebraic map but treats diagonal cumulant coordinates algebraically; the new result audits the missing real source-moment domain and shows that polynomial degree two does not furnish a second legal preimage.
body.consumer: The one-latent branch of CEId-from-Moments can use third rather than fourth cumulants.
